beats.text: The weighted sum can be any number: minus twelve, zero, three point seven. But for a class, we want a probability.
That is the job of the activation function. It takes the sum, and turns it into the unit's output.
For two classes, we use the sigmoid. It squeezes any number into the range zero to one.
A big positive sum gives almost one. A big negative sum gives almost zero. And a sum of exactly zero gives zero point five.
So one sigmoid output is read as the probability of class one. Choose class one when it is above zero point five: that is the same as the sum being above zero.
The slides list other common ones. tanh gives values from minus one to one. ReLU keeps a positive sum, and turns a negative one into zero. For regression, the output simply stays linear.
With more than two classes, the network has one output per class, and we use softmax.
Say the scores are two, one and zero. Raise e to each: about seven point three nine, two point seven two, and one.
Divide each by the total, eleven point one one. You get zero point six seven, zero point two four, and zero point zero nine.
They add up to one, and the network chooses class one, the largest. Because they share one total, the classes compete: raise one score, and the others fall.
But activations do something bigger. Look at XOR. It is one when exactly one input is one.
The two ones sit on one diagonal, the two zeros on the other. No single straight line can separate them.
So we add a hidden layer. One hidden unit draws one line, the other draws a second, and the output unit combines them.
This works only because each hidden unit applies its activation. Without it, the network is just sums of sums, and it collapses back into one line.
And when are they used? Not before training. They are part of the network. Every forward pass applies them, in training and in prediction, and backpropagation uses their slope.
For the exam.
The activation turns the sum into the output.
Sigmoid: one output, two classes.
Softmax: one output per class, summing to one.
Without activations, the layers collapse into one line.
They are used in training and in prediction.
